summary: Harden OpenClaw gateway startup and RDC self-heal against plugin-schema drift, orphaned Android gateway locks, required offline state migration, Node network-path mismatch and watchdog restart loops.
reason: A real outage combined installed-plugin schema drift, an orphaned gateway lock that Android Node misclassified because kill(0) returned EPERM, and an RDC remote fetch timeout that curl did not reproduce.

tests.name: gateway-preflight
tests.evidence: 8/8 self-contained Tier-0 gateway preflight tests passed, covering schema drift, missing installed manifest, unsupported config, reversible stale-lock quarantine, live owner, PID reuse, active listener and run.sh preflight order.

tests.name: remote-desktop-watchdog
tests.evidence: 19/19 tests passed, including scoped IPv4-first Node environment, same-stack dependency probe and persistent circuit backoff across watchdog restart.

tests.name: rdc-incident-loop
tests.evidence: 5/5 incident-loop tests passed; verified repair remains bounded and replay-safe.

tests.name: live-read-only-preflight
tests.evidence: Current plugin schema returned ok; current gateway lock returned active_owner; OpenClaw healthz live and RDC functional health healthy.

tests.name: companion-maintenance-recovery
tests.evidence: Deterministic compiled Companion test passed: detects only maintenance markers; skips Doctor when already recovered; refuses live gateway ownership; retries Doctor at most twice; caller cannot widen the two-attempt budget.

tests.name: companion-build-and-regression
tests.evidence: TypeScript build and existing Companion run-control regression passed on the isolated candidate.

capabilities.reason: Existing recovery owners and entrypoints are unchanged; deterministic admission, offline maintenance repair, same-stack reachability and bounded retry semantics are strengthened.

architecture.reason: No new daemon, scheduler, router, database, orchestrator or source of truth. Existing Companion, Health Manager, RDC controller/watchdog and Tier-0 owners are retained.

rollback: Revert this maintenance commit and promote the previous immutable Tier-0 runtime release.
limitations: This change does not alter OpenClaw's upstream process.kill(pid,0) EPERM semantics globally; the Termux runtime preflight applies the safer recovery decision at the canonical S24 gateway entrypoint.

Automatic Doctor repair runs only after the exact startup maintenance marker, is time-bounded, refuses concurrent gateway ownership, and retries startup once; other failures remain on the canonical incident path.
Gateway startup can remain slow under high session materialization or memory pressure; that performance concern is separate from this outage hardening.
